questions.question: What core motivation drives parameter-efficient finetuning (PEFT) for large pretrained models in practical settings?
questions.choice_A: To enable adaptation to many tasks without duplicating the full set of base parameters for each task
questions.choice_B: To eliminate the need for any labeled data during adaptation
questions.choice_C: To guarantee zero-shot performance equal to supervised finetuning
questions.choice_D: To replace pretraining so that models can be trained entirely on downstream data

questions.question: Compared to full finetuning, which cost is most directly reduced by PEFT methods when deploying many task-specific models?
questions.choice_A: The cost of collecting pretraining corpora
questions.choice_B: The storage footprint per task because only small task-specific parameters are stored
questions.choice_C: The number of forward passes required per batch
questions.choice_D: The cost of decoding at test time in beam search

questions.question: In the context of adapters, what is the typical structural change introduced into a Transformer layer?
questions.choice_A: Replacing the attention mechanism with a convolutional module
questions.choice_B: Doubling the hidden dimension of the feedforward network
questions.choice_C: Inserting a small bottleneck subnetwork with its own parameters while freezing the original layer
questions.choice_D: Removing layer normalization to reduce parameter counts

questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes prompt tuning from prefix tuning?
questions.choice_A: Prompt tuning modifies the attention heads, while prefix tuning modifies only biases
questions.choice_B: Prompt tuning learns task-specific linear layers, while prefix tuning freezes all weights including embeddings
questions.choice_C: Prompt tuning learns soft token embeddings prepended at the input, while prefix tuning learns key-value vectors injected into each layer’s attention
questions.choice_D: Prompt tuning requires finetuning all layers, while prefix tuning requires no training

questions.question: In Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), which description of the weight update is most accurate for adapting a weight matrix $W \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{out} \times d_{in}}$?
questions.choice_A: The update is factorized as $\Delta W = B A$ with $B \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{out} \times r}$ and $A \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_{in}}$, where $r \ll \min(d_{out}, d_{in})$
questions.choice_B: The update sets $W$ to a diagonal matrix keeping only the largest singular value
questions.choice_C: The update is applied by sparsifying $W$ with a fixed threshold
questions.choice_D: The update replaces $W$ with a random orthogonal matrix

questions.question: What is a practical deployment benefit of LoRA compared to adapters?
questions.choice_A: LoRA requires no additional computation during training
questions.choice_B: LoRA updates can be merged into the base weights after training to avoid extra inference latency
questions.choice_C: LoRA guarantees better accuracy than full finetuning on any task
questions.choice_D: LoRA does not require choosing any hyperparameters

questions.question: BitFit is characterized by which minimal-parameter strategy?
questions.choice_A: Training only the layer normalization scales
questions.choice_B: Training only the attention projection matrices
questions.choice_C: Training only the bias terms across the network
questions.choice_D: Training only the embedding matrix

questions.question: Which trade-off commonly arises when choosing the rank $r$ in LoRA?
questions.choice_A: Higher $r$ reduces capacity but improves latency
questions.choice_B: Lower $r$ improves capacity but increases memory usage
questions.choice_C: Higher $r$ increases capacity but also increases parameter count and potential latency if unmerged
questions.choice_D: Rank has no effect on either performance or efficiency

questions.question: Which metric best captures the deployment advantage of PEFT when serving many tasks from a single base model?
questions.choice_A: Number of trainable parameters per task that must be stored and loaded at inference
questions.choice_B: Number of attention heads in the base model
questions.choice_C: Vocabulary size of the tokenizer
questions.choice_D: Number of training epochs during pretraining

questions.question: Why might adapters increase inference latency compared to LoRA that has been merged into the base weights?
questions.choice_A: Adapters require more decoding steps for autoregressive models
questions.choice_B: Adapters add extra layers or projections in the forward pass that cannot be eliminated without retraining
questions.choice_C: Adapters increase the sequence length
questions.choice_D: Adapters require beam search

questions.question: Which statement about prompt length in prompt tuning is typically true with respect to latency?
questions.choice_A: Longer prompts reduce latency because they regularize the model
questions.choice_B: Longer prompts do not affect latency because they are ignored during attention
questions.choice_C: Longer prompts can increase latency due to longer input sequences and attention computation
questions.choice_D: Prompt length only affects training time, not inference time

questions.question: In prefix tuning for Transformers, what is being optimized per layer?
questions.choice_A: Only the output projection of attention
questions.choice_B: Randomly initialized positional encodings that remain fixed
questions.choice_C: Trainable key and value vectors that are concatenated to the true keys and values
questions.choice_D: The entire feedforward block with frozen attention

questions.question: Which scenario best highlights the storage advantage of PEFT over full finetuning?
questions.choice_A: Serving 100 tasks where each task’s parameters are less than 1% of the base model size
questions.choice_B: Serving 1 task with extremely high throughput requirements
questions.choice_C: A single offline evaluation of a model on a public benchmark
questions.choice_D: Training a model from scratch on massive web-scale data

questions.question: What is a common initialization choice for LoRA that helps preserve the base model’s function at the start of finetuning?
questions.choice_A: Initialize $A$ and $B$ so that $\Delta W$ is approximately zero, often by setting one factor to zero
questions.choice_B: Initialize $A$ as identity and $B$ as identity
questions.choice_C: Initialize $W$ to zero before applying LoRA
questions.choice_D: Initialize $A$ and $B$ from a large Gaussian to accelerate learning

questions.question: Orthogonality-based finetuning approaches aim to mitigate interference with prior knowledge primarily by:
questions.choice_A: Maximizing gradient norms across tasks
questions.choice_B: Constraining updates or gradients to be orthogonal to subspaces associated with previous tasks
questions.choice_C: Replacing attention with recurrence
questions.choice_D: Pruning neurons with low activation

questions.question: Which evaluation practice best isolates the parameter efficiency of different PEFT methods?
questions.choice_A: Comparing accuracy while allowing each method to use arbitrary parameter budgets
questions.choice_B: Comparing on the same tasks with matched trainable parameter counts and reporting performance, memory, and latency
questions.choice_C: Comparing pretraining perplexity only
questions.choice_D: Comparing wall-clock time on different hardware and batch sizes

questions.question: Which modules are commonly targeted by LoRA in Transformer architectures for strong performance–efficiency trade-offs?
questions.choice_A: Only layer normalization scales
questions.choice_B: Only the embedding matrix
questions.choice_C: Attention projections (e.g., $W_Q, W_K, W_V, W_O$) and sometimes feedforward projections
questions.choice_D: Only output softmax layer

questions.question: Which failure mode is most likely if the LoRA rank $r$ is set too low for a complex downstream task?
questions.choice_A: Overfitting due to too much capacity in the low-rank factors
questions.choice_B: Underfitting because the low-rank update cannot express the needed adaptation
questions.choice_C: Exploding gradients due to orthogonal constraints
questions.choice_D: Catastrophic forgetting of pretraining due to full-weight updates

questions.question: When comparing BitFit to prompt tuning at the same trainable parameter budget, which difference is most relevant?
questions.choice_A: BitFit changes internal computations via biases, while prompt tuning modifies the inputs seen by the model
questions.choice_B: Both modify only the embedding matrix
questions.choice_C: Both add per-layer key-value caches
questions.choice_D: BitFit always yields lower latency because it shortens sequences

questions.question: Which practical consideration often favors PEFT methods for multi-tenant serving in production?
questions.choice_A: PEFT methods eliminate the need for gradient checkpoints during training
questions.choice_B: PEFT methods allow dynamic swapping of small task-specific parameter sets on a shared base model, reducing memory and startup times
questions.choice_C: PEFT methods guarantee identical throughput to the base model regardless of sequence length
questions.choice_D: PEFT methods can only be used with encoder-only architectures
